sources.title: Differential Synchronization
sources.locator: §1 three-way exchange paragraph; §2 failed patch paragraph; §3 Dual Shadow; §4 Guaranteed Delivery / Asymmetry
sources.bounded_excerpt: This will destroy all changes since the previous successful synchronization.
sources.reviewer_observation: Simple shadow recovery can discard edits. Guaranteed delivery adds versioned acknowledgments, retransmission queues and backup shadows; peer symmetry changes backup requirements. Failed fuzzy patches can be reversed out. The half-duplex criticism concerns the described discard-on-in-flight-edit exchange.

sources.title: GNU Diffutils: common-ancestor merge
sources.locator: §8; §8.1 Selecting Which Changes to Incorporate; §8.2 Marking Conflicts; §8.3 Generating the Merged Output Directly; §14.1 Options to diff3
sources.bounded_excerpt: If you specify -m without an ed script option, -A is assumed.
sources.reviewer_observation: Argument order is mine, older, yours. -e/-E omit already matching tips; -A includes conflicts where only the ancestor differs. -m defaults to -A unless an edit-script option is supplied. GNU overlap has a technical three-different-files meaning; same-region changes and user-escalation policy must not be treated as universal tool semantics. The manual validates the edition/date lead, not decades of unchanged behavior.
sources.applicability: Checks discovery.md lines 13, 23, 32. Prevents an incorrect reviewer allegation that default -m always accepts identical concurrent changes.
